paths.title: Mathematics foundation
paths.summary: Start with calculus and linear algebra; every later analysis course assumes both.

steps.why: Limits, derivatives, integrals and series — the calculation base for everything after.
Vector spaces and matrices, shared by analysis, probability and machine learning.

paths.title: Analysis track
paths.summary: Move from the algebra-and-analysis course into measure theory, then use probability to test the abstraction.

steps.why: Settle notation for sets, maps and limits first.
Measures and measurable functions, the axiomatic base of probability.
Revisit probability inside the measure framework to check the abstractions land.

paths.title: Partial differential equations
paths.summary: Take ordinary differential equations and analysis first, then PDEs.

steps.why: Existence and solution methods for ODEs are the prerequisite.
Start from the heat and fluid equations, with characteristics.

paths.title: Quantum mechanics
paths.summary: Quantum mechanics uses linear algebra as its language; get matrices and inner products first.

steps.why: State vectors, operators and basis changes are linear algebra.
Old quantum theory through path integrals, with worked problems.

paths.title: AI toolchain
paths.summary: Begin with skill orchestration, then add web access and 3D work; run each locally before wiring it in.

steps.why: Turn scattered skills into a reproducible pipeline first.
Give that pipeline a reliable way to read the web.
When you need 3D work, keep the same quality gate on output.

paths.title: General chemistry
paths.summary: Start with thermodynamics and electrochemistry, then the kinetics derivations.

steps.why: Definition/proposition/example structure makes it a good first chemistry course.
